assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised with strontium by Katori and Ye, moved timekeeping to fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, about two orders better than the caesium standard. This is a clear case of what can be measured and how accurately. The work enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. Impact is broad and the principle is easy to state.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice concept and early Sr demonstrations; Ye drove the systematic-uncertainty and coherence record. A two-person prize is clean. Contributions of other groups (e.g. Ytterbium and Al+ clocks, NIST, PTB, and the frequency-comb link already honoured in 2005) are acknowledged but not obviously decisive for this discovery.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce the performance. Clocks are mature, though the SI redefinition has not yet happened, so recognition rests on demonstrated performance rather than adoption.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as invention/technique or discovery; the comb-clock link to the 2005 prize could be read as overlap.
Exact attribution of the lattice-clock idea relative to other early proposers is from memory and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller 1995 proposal for quantum gates with laser-cooled trapped ions, and its experimental realisation, established a leading platform for quantum computation and simulation, with high-fidelity gates and entangling operations. It is conceptually original and had large downstream impact on quantum information hardware.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal; Blatt led the experimental gate and entanglement demonstrations in Innsbruck. Wineland and Haroche were recognised in 2012 for ion and photon control, so the remaining credit is plausibly this trio, but Wineland's NIST gate work and Monroe's contributions complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of confirmation across several groups and companies. Timing is good since the platform is now commercial.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize scope and the Wineland/Monroe contributions.
B044 on the longlist covers largely the same people; only this entry is ranked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 quantum key distribution turned quantum measurement limits into a cryptographic protocol, and led to a field with fibre and satellite implementations. The idea is original and lasting, and connects foundations with technology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the originators of BB84. Ekert's entanglement-based protocol is also important, and Pan's group led the satellite and network demonstrations; including all four exceeds the three-person limit and the protocol stage versus the engineering stage are different contributions. I propose the originators.
assessment.maturity: Protocol is decades old and widely demonstrated, but practical security against implementation attacks and real-world deployment remain evolving. The 2022 prize on Bell tests and entangled photons partly adjoins this area.
uncertainties: Whether the Ekert contribution should displace one of the BB84 authors.
Physics content versus computer-science/cryptography content for a physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise tunable Hubbard models, with the superfluid-Mott transition, single-site quantum gas microscopy and quantum simulation of many-body states. This opened a laboratory for quantum many-body physics with exceptional control, building on laser cooling and BEC recognised earlier.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch-Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch observed the Mott transition, and Greiner and Bloch developed quantum gas microscopes. Credit is shared across many groups (Hänsch, Kasevich, Esslinger, Weiss, others), so a three-person selection is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent groups; the field is mature, though the scientific payoff for solving open condensed-matter problems is still developing.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among a large community.
Whether quantum simulation advantage beyond classical methods is considered established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical addressing and coherent control of single spins in diamond colour centres (NV and others) enabled room-temperature quantum sensing, spin-photon interfaces and small quantum registers. This resonates strongly with my own field of optical coherence in solids, and the measurement connection is direct.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup demonstrated optically detected single NV spins; Awschalom led coherent control and the broader solid-state spin programme; Lukin contributed coherent interfaces and sensing with NV centres. Others (Hanson, Jelezko, Walsworth, Budker) made major contributions, so allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strong replication and a broad range of applications, from nanoscale magnetometry to quantum networks; the field remains in active development.
uncertainties: Allocation among several comparably credible leaders.
Disclosure: my own work on rare-earth-ion crystals is adjacent, though not the same system.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, providing the readout and control architecture of superconducting quantum processors. The impact is substantial and well demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf are the theory-plus-experiment core of the 2004 proposal and demonstration (with Girvin and Huang). Schoelkopf's group also developed the transmon with Yale colleagues, and Girvin's omission is a point of unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with very broad confirmation. However, the Academy recently recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, which makes near-term recognition of an adjacent topic less likely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently honoured superconducting-circuit work.
Girvin and other contributors are not on the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire gain media, Kerr-lens mode-locking and semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors made compact solid-state femtosecond lasers routine and are the backbone of ultrafast science, spectroscopy and frequency combs. It is strongly enabling, though more of an invention than a discovery.
assessment.attribution: Moulton for Ti:sapphire, Sibbett's group for Kerr-lens mode-locking, Keller for SESAM and carrier-envelope control. The clean split among inventors is plausible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Technology is decades old and ubiquitous; Nobel prizes for attosecond pulses (2023) and chirped-pulse amplification (2018) already cover neighbouring territory, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2018 and 2023 prizes in ultrafast optics.
Who among Sibbett and others first demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking is from memory and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical-tweezer arrays of Rydberg atoms provide programmable quantum simulators and emerging neutral-atom quantum processors, with demonstrations of quantum phases, entanglement and logical-qubit operation. It is a rapidly maturing platform and an elegant combination of AMO techniques.
assessment.attribution: Browaeys and Lukin led large-scale programmable array experiments, while Saffman and Zoller made key proposals for Rydberg blockade gates. With four credited, the leaders for the experimental platform are best chosen, but the theory origin (Jaksch, Lukin, Zoller) may deserve recognition.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young; the key results are within the last decade and the scalability of error-corrected operation is still being tested, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the long record of other candidates.
Distribution of credit among theorists and experimenters.
